hints: List canonical Roman value-symbol pairs in descending order.
Always take the largest pair that fits the remaining value.
Repeat the current pair while it fits, then continue to the next smaller pair.
Stop when the remaining value reaches zero.
title: Integer to Roman Problem

notes: Use the standard subtractive pairs only: IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM.
A greedy loop over value→symbol pairs from largest to smallest is simple, correct, and optimal for the bounded input range.
Output must be an exact JSON string (including surrounding quotes) matching the expected Roman numeral.
constraints: Input is an integer within the inclusive range 1..3999
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of one integer: [num]. Example: [1994]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialized string containing the Roman numeral, e.g. "MCMXCIV"
content.problemStatement:
Convert an integer to its Roman numeral representation using standard modern Roman numeral rules.

Roman numerals use the following symbols and values:

| Symbol | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| I | 1 |
| V | 5 |
| X | 10 |
| L | 50 |
| C | 100 |
| D | 500 |
| M | 1000 |

Rules (modern usage):
- Symbols are placed from largest to smallest, left to right, and their values are added.
- To avoid four identical symbols in a row, subtractive notation is used for these specific pairs only: 4 (IV), 9 (IX), 40 (XL), 90 (XC), 400 (CD), 900 (CM).

With an integer `num`, output its Roman numeral representation as a string. The input is guaranteed to be in the range 1..3999 inclusive.

Recommended approach: greedy decomposition using a sorted list of value→symbol pairs (largest to smallest).

notes: All hidden testcases use the same JSON input protocol.
All expected outputs are exact Roman numeral strings.
No generator testcases are required because the input domain is small and bounded.
All hidden inputs satisfy the inclusive constraint 1..3999.
The greedy ordering directly enforces canonical Roman numeral construction.
Only IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, and CM are used as subtractive pairs.
solution.approach: Use greedy decomposition with the canonical Roman numeral value-symbol pairs ordered from largest to smallest. Repeatedly append the corresponding symbol while its value fits and subtract that value from num.

better.complexity: O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space for the fixed 1..3999 range, excluding the output string.
better.description: Use compact digit-to-Roman lookup tables for each decimal position. Each decimal digit is converted independently and the four fragments are concatenated.

optimal.complexity: O(1) time for 1..3999 and O(1) auxiliary space excluding the output string.
optimal.description: Iterate through the canonical value-symbol pairs [1000,M], [900,CM], [500,D], [400,CD], [100,C], [90,XC], [50,L], [40,XL], [10,X], [9,IX], [5,V], [4,IV], and [1,I]. Append a symbol while its value fits, then subtract it.

bruteForce.complexity: O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space for the fixed 1..3999 range, excluding the output string.
bruteForce.description: Use four lookup tables for thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones, then concatenate the Roman fragment for each decimal digit.

solution.timeComplexity: O(1) for the stated bounded input range because the algorithm scans a fixed list of 13 canonical value-symbol pairs.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space excluding the output string.

followUps: How would you extend the method for an expanded Roman numeral convention beyond 3999?
How does a digit-table solution compare with the greedy solution?

hidden.label: Multiple subtractive pairs at high magnitude

learningObjectives: Validate exact string outputs at numeric boundaries.
